title: Matrices and Transformations
scope: Use rectangular arrays to organize datasets and transform vectors with transparent arithmetic.
beginnerEntry: You can interpret, add, and scale vectors.

objectives: Identify matrix rows, columns, and shape.
Interpret a matrix as data and as a transformation.
Connect matrices to batches of feature vectors.

steps.prompt: A table has three customers as rows and age and visits as columns. What does its 3 by 2 shape communicate before reading any values?
How can the same rectangular array both store observations and describe a rule that transforms a vector?
Predict how [[2,0],[0,3]] changes vector (4,5), then describe the visual effect on horizontal and vertical components.
A matrix has ordered rows and columns. Multiplying it by a vector forms each output from a row-weighted sum, producing a repeatable linear transformation.
Compute [[1,2],[3,0]] times (4,5) by hand, labeling every product and sum. Then find one rectangular table in your own day, a timetable, spreadsheet, or menu, and name what its rows and columns mean.
The photo on your screen is a matrix of pixel numbers. A spreadsheet of 1,000 customers with 5 columns is a 1000 by 5 matrix. The same object stores an image and a dataset.
A graphics engine rotates a game character by multiplying every corner point by one matrix. What would it mean to apply one transformation matrix to every row of a customer dataset at once?
Weights (0.5, 2) turn (hours studied, sleep hours) into one readiness score via a weighted sum. Predict the scores for (4, 8) and (10, 2), and predict which habit the weights reward more.

A machine-learning layer is exactly this: a weight matrix multiplying feature vectors, turning raw measurements into scores. Whole datasets flow through as matrix products, the same row-weighted sums you did by hand, repeated at scale.

Compute the readiness score [[0.5, 2]] times (6, 7) by hand, labeling each product and sum, and state what the score means. Notice the limitation: these transformations are exact, but real measurements are noisy and outcomes are not guaranteed. Arithmetic alone cannot say probably. That needs probability.

measurement.prePrompt: Explain what rows, columns, and shape mean in a rectangular table of numbers.
measurement.postPrompt: Interpret a 2 by 3 matrix, verify whether it can multiply a length-3 vector, compute the result, and connect the operation to feature weighting.
successCriteria: States matrix shape in rows by columns.

misconceptions: Matrix dimensions may be read in either order.
Any two shapes can be multiplied.
Rows and columns need no semantic labels.
reasoning.tutorGuidance: Start with shape and labels, then trace one output cell as a dot product between one row and the input vector. Do not allow memorized multiplication without dimensional meaning.
